pr_title: feat(terminal): add commands to control terminal panel's position
pr_body:
* Add three new actions to `TerminalPanel` – `DockRight`, `DockBottom` and `DockLeft` – which allows controlling the terminal panel's position.

Closes #23115 

Release Notes:

- Added commands to set the terminal panel's dock position.

issue_context.title: Commands to change panel's dock position
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [X] Completed

### Describe the feature

When switching between using Zed in an external monitor and on a 14" MacBook Pro I usually move the Terminal Panel's position from the right dock to the bottom. Another situation where this usually happens is if I want to have both the Assistant Panel as well as the Terminal Panel open at the same time, meaning they can't be in the same dock position (if I'm not mistaken).

At the moment, if we want to change the Terminal Panel's position, one needs to right-click the Terminal Panel's icon in the status bar and then select the new desired position. 

Since I'm a big fan of being able to use the keyboard to, pretty much, use and control every aspect of my editor I'm proposing adding commands to the Command Palette that allows users to control the Terminal Panel's position without having to use the mouse.

P.S.: I guess the same could be done for the Assistant Panel, or any panel for that matter, so that in the future any panel's position could be controlled from the command palette.

### Zed Version and System Specs

Zed: v0.168.3 (Zed)
OS: macOS 15.0.0
Memory: 16 GiB
Architecture: aarch64

### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help present your vision of the feature


Here's a quick video of a quick implementation 🔽 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2c1bdb7-2651-4df7-ad20-96d6b8345b19

It simply adds three new commands to the command palette:

* `terminal panel: dock left` – Sets the Terminal Panel's position to the left dock.
* `terminal panel: dock bottom` – Sets the Terminal Panel's position to the bottom dock.
* `terminal panel: dock right` – Sets the Terminal Panel's position to the right dock.

Hey there @SomeoneToIgnore 👋 

Hope you don't mind me tagging you but I thought a little bit more about the feedback you kindly provided in https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/23116 and tried a different approach, which I wanted to share with you to see if it makes more sense, and only then, if applicable, open a Pull Request.

You can check this initial draft commit with the new approach –https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/commit/f8a823121383f2ea2719863aedf16d79eca77920 – but here's a quick breakdown of what is happening:

1. Added a new `next_position` method with a default implementation to the `Panel` trait
    * This default implementation simply finds the valid dock positions for the panel, leveraging  the `position_is_valid` method, and then updates the panel's position to the next valid position.
    * Since it takes into consideration the result of `position_is_valid`, it also works for panels that can't be docked at the bottom, like the Outline Panel.
2. For each panel that is meant to have this command, a new `NextDockPosition` action is registered, which simply calls the `next_position` default implementation
    * Only added it to `TerminalPanel` and `OutlinePanel` for demonstration purposes.
    * This follows somewhat the same approach of the `ToogleFocus`, where all (AFAIK) panels define the action but each have their own implementation of how to handle that action.
    * Since we have a default implementation for `next_position`, I guess we could also have a "default" `NextDockPosition` action that all panels "inherit" from the `Panel` trait, but I'm not sure if that's doable or if it even makes sense to do so.

Here's a quick video of it in action 🔽 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0a99029-c960-473c-8a1e-b174c630f78b

Let me know if you think this approach makes more sense! Also happy to try other approaches if you think there's a better way to do this 🙂

Nice progress, I like `fn next_position` placement.
As a small style nit, I would've written it a bit differently, to avoid extra allocations:
```rs
let next_position = [
    DockPosition::Left,
    DockPosition::Bottom,
    DockPosition::Right,
]
.into_iter()
.filter(|position| self.position_is_valid(*position))
.skip_while(|valid_position| valid_position != current_position)
.nth(1)
.unwrap_or(DockPosition::Left)
```

Also, since you move the panel in the same method, it could be renamed into `toggle_position` or `move_to_next_position` or whatever you find suitable.
`fn next_position` is named so, that I'd expect it to return a position, without moving.

-----------------

As for registering it per each panel, I do not think this is the right way: I would rather register this in the workspace, something similar to https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/bd3f64c5a148b67bcbd833b5ec98c79f740ce838/crates/workspace/src/workspace.rs#L4492

The workspace is able to access Docks already, e.g. https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/bd3f64c5a148b67bcbd833b5ec98c79f740ce838/crates/workspace/src/workspace.rs#L4536-L4540

so we can write another method with something like "if the dock is open and active, use that Dock method to move it to the next position".

The only "tough" issue I see is to understand which dock to apply this action to, but the same `pub fn toggle_dock` operates focus listeners (`active_panel.focus_handle(cx).contains_focused(cx)`) which should be enough.

> As a small style nit, I would've written it a bit differently, to avoid extra allocations:
> 
> ```rust
> let next_position = [
>     DockPosition::Left,
>     DockPosition::Bottom,
>     DockPosition::Right,
> ]
> .into_iter()
> .filter(|position| self.position_is_valid(*position))
> .skip_while(|valid_position| valid_position != current_position)
> .nth(1)
> .unwrap_or(DockPosition::Left)
> ```

Nice! I appreciate these style nits. I'm relatively new to Rust, so this helps me become more aware of how to write better Rust code. 🙂

> Also, since you move the panel in the same method, it could be renamed into `toggle_position` or `move_to_next_position` or whatever you find suitable.
> `fn next_position` is named so, that I'd expect it to return a position, without moving.

If you're okay with it, I'll use move_to_next_position, mainly because I associate the word "toggle" with something that can change between two states. For example, the ToggleFocus action either brings a panel into focus or removes focus from it. In this case, since some panels can have one of three possible positions, using move_to instead of toggle might make the intent clearer.

Lastly, thank you so much for the pointers at the end of your comment! I'll explore those suggestions and the codebase a bit more, and hopefully push another commit to my branch with your suggested approach. 👍

Hey there @SomeoneToIgnore 👋 

I've reviewed the implementation and have pushed another commit – https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/commit/22c70cfe91482b09f7d5d4d1a26d186cdb82b8e0 – with the suggested changes for the `move_to_next_position` method as well as the new approach.

The detail is present in the commit's message but I'll also leave it here for your convinience:

* Remove the `NextDockPosition` action that had been introduced to both `TerminalPanel` and `OutlinePanel`, in favour of a `MoveFocusePanelToNextPosition` action in the workspace namespace.
* Move the `move_to_next_position` default method implementation from the `Panel` trait to the `PanelHandle` trait, as that is the type of the value returned by `Dock::active_panel`.
* Introduce the `Workspace::move_focused_panel_to_next_position` method, which is triggered by the `MoveFocusedPanelToNextPosition` action and will find the currently focused panel in the currently focused dock and move that panel to the next dock position.

As you can see, the implementation changes a little bit from the original where, instead of having a command per panel (`terminal panel: move to next position`, `outline panel: move to next position`, etc.) there's now a single command – `workspace: move focused panel to next position` – and if there's no focused panel, nothing changes.

Here's a quick video of it in action 🔽 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/264d382b-5239-40aa-bc5e-5d569dec0734

Let me know what you think and thank you for the help so far! 🙂
